title: Pseudorabies Virus Injection into Spleen and Mesenteric Lymph Nodes
author: Kavi Rude
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfhfjj3n

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the induction chamber, close the lid, and deliver isoflurane and O2 via stopcock valves.

substeps.instruction: Observe for slower respiratory rate, loss of balance, and slowed movement.
Remove the mouse from the chamber once it becomes recumbent and non-responsive (approximately 3 minutes).

steps.title: Maintain Anesthesia and Prepare Eyes
steps.instruction: Maintain anesthesia using a nose cone and protect the eyes.

substeps.instruction: Place the mouse in dorsal recumbency on the shaving station pad.
Place the nose cone over the nose and adjust stopcock valves to redirect Isoflurane and O2 flow from the induction chamber to the nose cone.
If necessary, secure the nose with a suture strap under the front central incisors tied to the nose cone.
Apply ample sterile eye lubricant to each eye, ensuring it remains during nose cone insertion.

steps.title: Prepare the Surgical Site
steps.instruction: Shave the target area and disinfect the skin.

substeps.instruction: Use a charged shaver to remove hair on the left side from above the hip to the left forelimb insertion.
For splenic injections: Shave width extending over the margins of the latissimus dorsi muscle.
For MLN injections: Shave lower, roughly over the caudal external abdominal oblique muscles.
Clean the incision site first with alcohol and then chlorhexidine, wiping in a spiral from the center outward (clean to dirty).

steps.title: Perform Initial Incisions
steps.instruction: Create an opening to access the abdominal cavity.

substeps.instruction: Grasp skin along the coronal midline with forceps and make a ~7mm incision through skin, subcutaneous tissue, and fascia over the target organ.
Separate skin from the abdominal cavity lining by gently opening closed scissors between layers, angling blades up and away from the body cavity.
Make a second incision underneath the first through the linea alba, transversalis fascia, and peritoneum lining, angling scissors up and away from viscera.
For spleen targets: Cut caudal to the spleen.

steps.title: Expose Target Organ
steps.instruction: Locate and expose the spleen or mesenteric lymph nodes (MLN).

substeps.instruction: For Spleen: Visualize through the body cavity lining once skin is peeled back.
For MLN: Use closed forceps to gently pull up the intestinal mesentery to expose the abdominal aorta; spread the mesentery 'fan' to locate the chain of lymph nodes.
If flipping mesentery for MLN visualization, note the direction of twist (usually counterclockwise) to restore original orientation before closure.

steps.title: Inject Pseudorabies Virus
steps.instruction: Inject the target organ while holding the body cavity lining away with forceps.

substeps.instruction: For Spleen: Perform three injections spread along the length of the organ.
For MLN: Perform one single injection.

steps.title: Close the Incision
steps.instruction: Verify organ placement and close the abdominal wall and skin.

substeps.instruction: Examine internal organ orientation to ensure all organs are intact and correctly placed.
Close the linea alba: Use one cruciate suture if the incision is ≤1cm, or a line of simple interrupted sutures spaced 2-3mm apart if the incision is >1cm.
Free the skin from remaining fascia using scissors.
Raise the skin upward like a tent using forceps in both hands and apply staples with a space of about half a staple width between each.
Tighten staples with forceps or needle driver if needed; use a line of suture over any remaining skin puckers.

steps.title: Post-Operative Recovery
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in a recovery cage and monitor until fully awake.

substeps.instruction: Check the temperature of the heating pad; provide heat to only one half of the cage so the animal can move away from the source.
Place a clean paper towel as a barrier between the animal and the heated part of the cage (do not use bedding).
Place the animal in the cage in ventral or lateral recumbency.
Stay in the procedure room to monitor the mouse until it has completely recovered.
Return the animal to its home cage once it can walk freely and shows appropriate alertness and responsivity.
